summary: The `target == "npm-runtime"` branch in `impl bundle` (line 2112) is unreachable, and the 22-line `_bundle_npm_runtime` helper it guards (lines 2086-2107) is therefore dead. Evidence: I grepped the whole repo for callers of `bundle` — the only call site is `jac/jaclang/cli/commands/impl/build.impl.jac:68` (`return bundle(output=output, target=projection, fat=fat)`), which is itself gated one line earlier by `if projection in ["jab", "sealed", "binary", "wheel", "npm"]`, so `target` can never be `"npm-runtime"`. The CLI surface agrees: `jac/jaclang/cli/commands/build.jac:20` declares `choices=["jab", "sealed", "binary", "wheel", "npm", "source", "native"]` and the generated manifest (`jac/jaclang/cli/impl/manifest.impl.jac:166`) repeats the same list — `npm-runtime` appears nowhere. A repo-wide grep for the literal `npm-runtime` returns exactly two hits: this branch and one release-notes line. No test calls `bundle(...)` or `_bundle_npm_runtime(...)`. Deleting both the branch and the helper also drops the now-unused `framework` parameter plumbing (`runtime_pkg_name(framework)` / `build_runtime_to(..., framework=framework)`), which the single dead caller only ever passed as "".

Two methods on `CommandRegistry` are never called anywhere in the repo: `has_command` (impl line 37, declared at `jac/jaclang/cli/registry.jac:19`) and `get_groups` (impl line 53, declared at `registry.jac:24`). Evidence: a repo-wide grep for `has_command` returns exactly two hits — the declaration and this impl — with no `.has_command(` call site in any `.jac`, `.py`, or test file. A repo-wide grep for `get_groups` returns hits only for a *different*, module-level `get_groups` in `jac/jaclang/cli/manifest.jac:83` (implemented at `jac/jaclang/cli/impl/manifest.impl.jac:2219`, consumed by `jac/jaclang/cli/impl/mcp_manifest.impl.jac:9`) — no `registry.get_groups()` / `.get_groups(` call reaches the `CommandRegistry` method. The sibling `CommandRegistry.get_all` is genuinely live (`jac/jaclang/cli/gen_cli_manifest.jac:54`), so the object itself stays. Removal is a paired edit: drop both impls here and both stubs in `registry.jac`.

Inside `impl completions` (line 158), the local `import from jaclang.cli.command { ArgKind }` at line 161 binds a name the function body never references. Evidence: I read the whole function (lines 158-168) — its body uses only `shellcode`, `get_registry`, `_extract_commands`, `_install_completion`, and `console`; `ArgKind` appears nowhere between line 162 and the closing brace. The only code in this file that actually needs `ArgKind` is `_extract_commands` (lines 170-207), which performs its own local `import from jaclang.cli.command { ArgKind }` at line 171 before using it at lines 179, 182, and 190-191. Because Jac function-local imports do not leak into callees, deleting line 161 cannot break `_extract_commands`. One-line deletion, no signature change, no other file touched.

`CompletionItemKind` in type_utils.jac declares all 25 LSP completion-kind constants, but only 6 are ever referenced. The sole consumer is `completion_kind_from_sym` in type_system/impl/type_utils.impl.jac:303-322, whose match returns exactly Module, Function, Class, Enum, Variable, and Text. I grepped the whole repo for `CompletionItemKind\.\w+` and got 8 hits total: those 6 in type_utils.impl.jac, plus `lspt.CompletionItemKind.Keyword` in jaclang/langserve/impl/engine.impl.jac:611 and `lspt.CompletionItemKind.Variable` in a tool fixture — both of which resolve to the *separate* LSP enum defined at jac/jaclang/lsp/types.jac:62, not this one. The remaining 19 members (Method, Constructor, Field, Interface, Property, Unit, Value, Keyword, Snippet, Color, File, Reference, Folder, EnumMember, Constant, Struct, Event, Operator, TypeParameter) have zero references anywhere in the tree. Judgement is needed because the numeric values must stay LSP-spec-aligned for the 6 that remain, so the surviving members must keep their current integer literals rather than being renumbered.

`TypeCategory.Unbound` (types.jac:9) is declared but never referenced. I grepped the whole repo for `TypeCategory\.\w+` and collected every occurrence: Unknown, Never, Any, Module, TypeVar, Class, Function, Overload, Union and EnumMember all appear as `CATEGORY` ClassVar assignments in types.jac plus reads in type_evaluator.impl/type_evaluator.impl.jac:2637 and type_system/impl/types.impl.jac:439-513 — `Unbound` appears nowhere but its own declaration line. No `TypeBase` subclass sets `CATEGORY = TypeCategory.Unbound`, so no type value can ever carry it. Because the enum is an `IntEnum` with implicit auto-numbering, deleting the first member shifts every subsequent member's integer value, so this needs a human to confirm nothing serializes these ordinals (JIR caches, .jir sections) before removing it.

`TemplateRegistry.is_empty` and `TemplateRegistry.clear` (declared at lines 27-28, implemented at `jac/jaclang/project/impl/template_registry.impl.jac:107-113`) have zero callers anywhere. I grepped the whole repo for `registry.clear`, `registry.is_empty`, `get_template_registry().` and bare `.clear()`/`is_empty()`: the only `registry.clear()` hit is `jac/tests/runtimelib/client/test_react_native_target.jac:28`, which operates on the unrelated client *target* registry from `jaclang.runtimelib.client.targets.registry`; every `is_empty()` call site resolves to `DependencyPlan.is_empty` (`cli/commands/impl/project.impl.jac:873,1145`), `CapabilityClosure.is_empty` (test_capabilities.jac), `Changeset.is_empty` or `SchemaRules.is_empty` — none to `TemplateRegistry`. The registry is a process-global singleton (`glob _registry` at template_registry.jac:31) that is only ever populated by `initialize_template_registry`, never emptied or probed.

`ProviderRegistry.clear` (lines 606-609) has no callers. I grepped the whole repo for `registry.clear`, `_registry.clear`, `get_provider_registry().` and bare `.clear()`: the provider-registry hits are only `get_provider_registry().register(...)` (test_dependencies.jac:1078,1125), `.get_by_flag("--npm")` (runtimelib/client/cli.jac:285), `.get("python")` (providers.jac:624) and `.all()` (cli/commands/impl/project.impl.jac:892). The one `registry.clear()` in the tree (`jac/tests/runtimelib/client/test_react_native_target.jac:28`) targets the client *target* registry from `jaclang.runtimelib.client.targets.registry`, and the `__jac_sv._registry.clear()` calls in `jaclang/scale/tests/data/test_eager_spawn.jac` are a plain dict. Test teardown here uses `reset_provider_registry()` (providers.jac:631) instead, which nulls the singleton outright — that function is the live reset path and must stay.

Three `or`-chain fallbacks read keys out of `_call_params_config` that that dict can never contain, so they always evaluate to None and contribute nothing: `max_react_iterations` at lines 745 and 1629, and `max_tool_result_length` at line 1784. `_call_params_config` is the module-level glob set in `llm.jac:51` from `_byllm_config.get_call_params_config()`, whose implementation at `impl/config_loader.impl.jac:60-75` builds a fresh dict containing at most three keys — `max_output_retries` always, `temperature` only if present in jac.toml, `max_tokens` only if > 0 — and nothing else; it is a whitelist, not a passthrough, so a user putting `max_react_iterations` under `[byllm.call_params]` would have it dropped. I grepped the whole repo for both names: every real usage is a per-call or per-model parameter (`tests/fixtures/react_max_iterations.jac:19`, `react_max_iterations_finish_tool.jac:28`, `jac/jaclang/cli/ai_agent.jac:286,288`), which the first two links of each chain (`mt_run.call_params` / `self.call_params`) already cover, and the docs table at `docs/reference/plugins/byllm.md:823,827` lists them as `by llm(...)` options, not jac.toml keys. Each chain already ends in a literal default (`or 0`, `or 500`), so deleting the third link is behaviour-preserving.

Two `_model_config` lookups in `Model.postinit` can never hit: `_model_config.get("http_client", False)` at line 4 and `_model_config.get("native_tools")` at line 35. `_model_config` is the glob set in `llm.jac:50` from `_byllm_config.get_model_config()`, and that implementation (`impl/config_loader.impl.jac:48-58`) returns a freshly built dict with exactly five keys — `default_model`, `api_key`, `base_url`, `proxy`, `verbose` — so both lookups always return the hard-coded default (`False` and `None` respectively). I grepped the repo for `native_tools|http_client`: every genuine setter goes through the per-`Model` `config={...}` dict — `tests/test_byllm.jac:1757` (`config={"native_tools": True}`), `tests/fixtures/system_prompt_override/direct_http_model_call.jac:14` and `byllm/README.md:117` (`"http_client": True`) — which the outer `self.config.get(...)` already handles. Neither key appears in `get_default_config` or in the `[byllm.model]` schema in `plugin_config.jac`, confirming they were never jac.toml keys. The lines reduce to `self.config.get("http_client", False)` and `self.config.get("native_tools")` with identical behaviour.
